Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Recorded at: 2025-12-20T15:30:00Z (UTC)
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Mariner - Head of ML), Evan Cole (Mariner - Platform Eng), Sana Mirza (Mariner - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Mariner is evaluating an exit from their current hosted LLM provider and a partial move off a homegrown vLLM/TGI stack. Main themes: compatibility with existing prompts/evals, latency vs cost tradeoffs, private deployment (VPC/on-prem) requirements for sensitive data, and proving eval parity on a pilot. They asked for pricing, security docs, and a technical deep-dive with a benchmark run using their prompt set.

Topics (auto-detected):
- Migration path from OpenAI/Anthropic and in-house vLLM to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private
- Eval parity and quality regressions detection
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted API cost/latency tradeoffs
- Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Laura from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Diego Martinez, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Patel: Hi Laura, good thanks. We have a lot to cover, trying to figure out if we move off our current hosted path and also how to fold in some of our in-house stuff.
[00:12] Evan Cole: Morning — Evan here, mainly platform questions.
[00:14] Sana Mirza: Sana — security lead, I may jump in with compliance questions.
[00:18] Diego Martinez: Great. Quick agenda: 1) understand current stack and pain points, 2) discuss Redwood hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), 3) compatibility/eval parity with vLLM/TGI and OpenAI, 4) next steps and pilot. Sound OK?
[00:26] Priya: Sounds good. For context we run a mix: most traffic is on OpenAI right now for chat generation but we built a vLLM/TGI inference cluster for cost reasons for high-volume batch tasks. We're also running a small private cluster on prem for PII-sensitive pipelines. Main driver: cost and consistency — we've seen different output between the hosted provider and our in-house runs, and we need to decide whether to continue improving vLLM or move to a vendor that can handle both hosted and private.
[00:46] Laura: Great, helpful. What's your target latency and what does your traffic profile look like?
[00:50] Priya: For interactive chat we need p95 under 400ms for short prompts, usually 8-16 token responses for quick ops. For batch reranks and embeddings it's throughput oriented — 200-500 QPS at peak for some jobs.
[01:06] Evan: Also we have strict data residency requirements for some projects — EU-only for certain customers.
[01:10] Sana: And we need SOC 2 compliance, SAML SSO integration with Okta, audit logs, and KMS integration for key material. Also we may need an on-prem option for a couple of customers.
[01:21] Diego: That's helpful. On the compat side, can you clarify what you mean by "compatibility" — are you looking for exact token-for-token parity with OpenAI or functional parity where prompts produce equivalent intent and quality?
[01:32] Priya: We want eval parity. We have a 300-prompt eval suite and some downstream metrics. It's less about exact tokens and more about regression risk — if we adopt another backend, we need confidence outputs won't break production.
[01:44] Laura: Perfect. So pilot approach we usually recommend is: 1) run sample prompts against Redwood hosted and your current provider side-by-side, 2) run QoQ/regression checks on the eval set, 3) optionally test Dedicated and Private for latency/cost baselining.
[02:01] Priya: That sounds sensible. How do you handle things like KV cache and continuous batching vs our vLLM setup? We rely a lot on KV-cache savings for long chat contexts.
[02:12] Diego: Redwood runtime supports KV cache semantics — we do continuous caching and prefix caching optimizations. There may be slight behavioral differences in cache eviction policies compared to custom vLLM, but we expose knobs for cache TTL and chunking. Also our batching is adaptive to preserve latency SLOs.
[02:28] Evan: Ok can you run dedicated capacity that looks like our in-house cluster for throughput tests? We're trying to see if Dedicated can give us similar cost per token at 200 QPS.
[02:37] Diego: Yes, Dedicated is intended for reserved GPU pools. You can configure autoscale and burst capacity. For cost we can run a modeled TCO: host vs dedicated vs private. We'll provide a TCO worksheet.
[02:48] Priya: There are concerns about model variants — we used several OpenAI-family models and some Mistral forks, and the TGI stack has some custom weights we've tuned. How do you handle model formats and weights?
[03:00] Laura: We maintain a model catalog with Redwood-verified profiles. For custom weights we support common formats and can onboard your model artifacts; SE team can help with conversion. Diego, maybe you can speak to TGI/vLLM compatibility?
[03:11] Diego: Sure. We've onboarded vLLM and TGI-based artifacts before. Sometimes it's trivial — same weights — sometimes tokenization differences or custom ops cause mismatch. We do a compatibility pass: convert, run a suite of smoke tests, and then run eval parity. If there are custom kernels, we can either use our compatibility runtime or help you package a private runtime in Dedicated/Private. I should note sometimes names get munged in auto-transcription — I mean, custom kernels can create behavior drift, but it's usually solvable.
[03:38] Priya: Good to hear. On the security front, what does the Private deployment look like? Is the control plane managed or customer-managed?
[03:45] Laura: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option (VPC peering or on-prem bundle). You can keep data in your network, integrate with your KMS/HSM, and we provide audit logs and endpoint policies. For high-regulation customers we do an on-prem appliance.
[03:57] Sana: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs? We need to show compliance evidence to procurement. Also, can we get network diagrams for the private deployment?
[04:07] Laura: We are SOC 2 Type II and have an ISO summary — we'll share a redacted pack. We'll include network diagrams and KMS integration notes.
[04:16] Evan: For SAML SSO, do you support Okta SCIM provisioning and role-based access? We have teams with different permissions.
[04:22] Diego: Yes, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported on both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, it depends on the exact installer but we can integrate with your identity provider.
[04:30] Priya: Cost question — our finance org was skeptical because the hosted provider was cheap per token but unpredictable. How does Redwood help control cost?
[04:38] Laura: We provide cost controls: per-route quotas, token-level cost breakdown, batching/quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize, and suggestions for model variants. We can show a live console demo of token-level cost traces.
[04:48] Diego: Also quantization profiles can substantially reduce cost for Chat and embedding workloads. For Dedicated, reserved capacity produces a predictable monthly commit which helps finance.
[04:56] Evan: On the eval parity, what's the usual acceptance criteria? Are we looking for statistical parity or absolute match?
[05:02] Priya: Statistical parity on our eval suite with defined thresholds — e.g., less than 2% delta in top-level metrics and no critical regression on key intents.
[05:11] Laura: We can run the eval and produce a regression report with per-prompt diffs, confidence deltas, and a rollback/mitigation plan. Usually we do a canary rollout: start on a small % of traffic and watch the metrics.
[05:23] Priya: That mitigates our risk. For the pilot we'd want a 4-week scope: week 1 integration and smoke tests, week 2 eval parity runs, week 3 latency/cost baselining on Dedicated, week 4 final report + decision. Is that feasible?
[05:37] Diego: Yes that timeline is realistic. We'll need your prompt set and traffic profile. Also we'll ask for representative payloads for KV cache behavior.
[05:45] Laura: We'll prepare SOW language and a pilot pricing option. Any blockers from your side?
[05:50] Sana: A few items: we need to confirm data deletion policies, whether logs with PII are masked by default, and the KMS key escrow model. Also we need to know if audit logs are tamper-evident.
[06:03] Diego: For Hosted we have soft-delete and configurable retention; for Private you can fully control retention via your KMS and log collection. Audit logs are write-once in the hosted control plane and we provide integrity checks — we'll include technical detail in the security pack.
[06:18] Priya: Another thing: we use some proprietary tokenization tweaks in our TGI pipelines that slightly change behavior. If we move to Redwood, can we bring our tokenization?
[06:28] Diego: We can support custom tokenizers as part of the model onboarding. There are edge cases with tokenizer-embedding alignment but normally it's manageable. We'll catalog any delta in the eval report.
[06:38] Evan: For throughput testing on Dedicated, do you help run the benchmark or do we run it and send logs?
[06:44] Diego: We can run it jointly — Redwood runs an instrumented workload and we provide the tooling so your team can reproduce. We'll produce cost and latency breakdowns per-token and per-route.
[06:54] Priya: Great. Any known limitations moving from vLLM to your runtime?
[06:58] Diego: Mostly custom operator support and narrow ops not in our optimized kernels. We often rewrite or emulate those ops, it's a bit of engineering but we have a backlog of patches. Also sometimes there's subtle answer drift due to different sampling seeds — that's why we emphasize eval parity checks.
[07:14] Laura: Quick commercial note: for teams that want to keep lower costs long term we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity plus Redwood Optimize suggestions. If you need isolated control plane and full network isolation, Private is the route. Hosted is the fastest to get started.
[07:28] Priya: We probably need to pilot Hosted first to validate eval parity, then if successful test Dedicated for throughput and optionally Private for regulated customers.
[07:36] Sana: Timeline-wise procurement expects a vendor decision by the end of Q1 2026. Does that align?
[07:41] Laura: That aligns; pilot in January and a decision window in late February/March would fit.
[07:47] Evan: One last technical — how do you handle fallbacks if a model variant fails? We sometimes want to degrade gracefully to a cheaper model.
[07:54] Diego: We support routing policies and automatic fallback chains. You can route by latency, cost, or model family; we also support function/tool calling and structured outputs.
[08:04] Priya: OK let's recap next steps.
[08:07] Laura: Recap: We'll send pricing, SOW and security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS notes) by 2025-12-23. Diego will schedule a 60m technical deep dive and pilot setup in the week of 2026-01-05. Priya will provide the 300 prompt eval set plus traffic profile by 2025-12-27. We'll run a Hosted parity test, then Dedicated throughput tests, and produce a final regression and cost report.
[08:28] Priya: That works. Anything else?
[08:31] Sana: Please make sure security docs include the private deployment network diagrams and KMS integration specifics.
[08:36] Laura: Noted. We'll attach those.
[08:39] Evan: Can you also include a short checklist of integration tasks so our infra folks know what's needed for the pilot?
[08:45] Diego: Yes we'll include a runbook and an infra checklist — ports, certs, VNets, SSO config, etc.
[08:52] Laura: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials.
[08:56] Priya: Thanks Laura, Diego.
[08:58] Meeting end.
